own_scenes.family: Old school: DJs, MCs y fiestas del Bronx
own_scenes.desc: A finales de los setenta las crews de varios MCs en torno a un DJ (Three MC’s, L Brothers, Funky 4, Treacherous Three) competían por la originalidad y, tomando nota de los Temptations o los Jackson 5, convirtieron la fiesta del DJ en un concierto: el MC pasó a ser la estrella y los b-boys se hicieron MCs. Los Brothers Disco de Breakout y Baron, con su sound system «Mighty Mighty Sasquatch», acompañaban a los Funky 4, con MC Sha-Rock, primera MC mujer, que aprendió de Melle Mel; con Rodney C y Jazzy Jeff fueron los Funky 4 + 1. Kool Moe Dee (Treacherous Three) rapeaba rápido y con un vocabulario inusual. Los miembros cambiaban de grupo sin parar: los Salt and Pepper Whipper Whip y Dot-A-Rock pasaron de los Cold Crush a los Fantastic Five de Grand Wizzard Theodore. Para DMC, los chavales del Bronx y de Harlem World hablaban su idioma: «la CNN de la calle».

influences.name: Grandmaster Flash y el arte del DJ
Afrika Bambaataa y la Zulu Nation

refs.q: I became the first female MC as part of an all-male group
refs.para: I became the first female MC as part of an all-male group, and the first female MC to help move the culture forward [with] the style of rhyme and how we created the cadence, the back-and-forth.

refs.q: They was the ones giving the CNN way of life of the streets for the younger kids, because we wasn’t in the clubs yet.
refs.para: But the Funky 4s and the Moe Dees and the Busy Bee Starskis and the Cold Crush and the Jazzy Five MCs and the fuckin’ Soulsonic Force and Bambaataa and the Zulu Nation and the fucking Mean Machine, they spoke my language. They was the ones giving the CNN way of life of the streets for the younger kids, because we wasn’t in the clubs yet.

refs.q: We all intertwined, until we all just got with the right menu.
refs.para: Easy A.D. (Cold Crush Brothers): We all intertwined, until we all just got with the right menu. So you went in and out of groups. I remember when our DJ left and went back home to Jamaica from the As Salaam Brothers, DJ Rashid and I tried out for Islam’s group. Donald D made it and I didn’t. And I ran into my brother Tony Tone. I said, “I’m an MC.”
